marker_occlusion_one_corner.what_went_wrong: A single obscured corner marker caused degraded warping and shifted candidate bubbles between rows.
marker_occlusion_one_corner.regression_risk: Small changes in marker detection, warping, or thresholding can reintroduce cross-row bleed and MR artifacts.
marker_occlusion_one_corner.test_oracle: Candidate number must read exactly with no MR marker.

degraded_three_marker_skew.what_went_wrong: Three-marker homography left a systematic vertical offset that made zero-gap INT columns bleed into neighbors.
degraded_three_marker_skew.regression_risk: Consensus/recentering tweaks can silently fall back to dy=0 and restore wrong digits.
degraded_three_marker_skew.test_oracle: Known production candidate number must read exactly with no MR marker.

historical_candidate_misread_fixed.what_went_wrong: Historical pages were misread after degraded marker recovery, including wrong candidate digits and unstable edge answers.
historical_candidate_misread_fixed.regression_risk: CropOnMarkers fallback and recenter logic changes can shift columns back into ambiguous states.
historical_candidate_misread_fixed.test_oracle: Pinned candidate number and selected answer columns remain stable on replay.

marker_fail_closed_confidence_gate.what_went_wrong: Extremely degraded geometry could be forced through, risking silent wrong reads.
marker_fail_closed_confidence_gate.regression_risk: Relaxing confidence gates without safeguards can turn hard-fail sheets into incorrect scored outputs.
marker_fail_closed_confidence_gate.test_oracle: Case is routed to ErrorFiles and does not produce a scored result row.

folded_edge_partial_marker.what_went_wrong: Folded-edge scan caused widespread same-sign shift votes that were previously rejected as no-consensus.
folded_edge_partial_marker.regression_risk: Any tightening of dominant-sign clustering can reintroduce MR(89)-style candidate ambiguity.
folded_edge_partial_marker.test_oracle: Pinned folded-edge candidate number reads exact and contains no MR marker.

hard_batch_known_good.what_went_wrong: Hard-batch pages are sensitive to subtle changes in preprocessing and marker recovery paths.
hard_batch_known_good.regression_risk: Performance or heuristic refactors can drift outputs without obvious failures in synthetic tests.
hard_batch_known_good.test_oracle: Known-good candidate baselines remain unchanged across replay.
